reasoning: The proposal's exact design — hold the deception/sabotage task and monitor prompts fixed, vary the actor model family, and compare the CoT-vs-output-only detection gap per family — is already executed in "CoT Red-Handed: Stress Testing Chain-of-Thought Monitoring" (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2505.23575), which varies five open/closed actor families (DeepSeek-R1, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B, Claude Sonnet 3.7 Thinking, Grok 3 Mini) with fixed monitors and reports per-model CoT-vs-action-only catch rates, finding the gap is regime/model-dependent. The broader problem (is the CoT-minus-output / monitorability advantage architecture- and training-recipe-specific across families?) is further answered by MonitorBench (arXiv 2603.28590, multiple families incl. DeepSeek-R1, Claude, Kimi K2, GPT-OSS-120B, Llama 3.3) and "Can Reasoning Models Obfuscate Reasoning?" (arXiv 2510.19851), which report strong per-family differences (Claude high obfuscation, non-Claude near zero; DeepSeek-R1 most monitorable). The only genuinely under-covered angle is the narrow framing as a direct replication of the specific GPT-5 system-card numbers, which is a minor delta on top of an already well-established result, so this is largely addressed rather than fully solved.

evidence.title: CoT Red-Handed: Stress Testing Chain-of-Thought Monitoring
evidence.summary: Directly implements the proposal's design: holds task and monitor models fixed, varies the untrusted/actor reasoning model across five families (DeepSeek-R1, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B, Claude Sonnet 3.7 Thinking, Grok 3 Mini), and compares CoT vs action/output-only monitoring catch rates per actor model. Finds the CoT-minus-output gap is regime- and model-dependent (CoT helps on subtle tasks, can hurt on non-subtle ones), and a hybrid monitor beats both.

evidence.title: MonitorBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Chain-of-Thought Monitorability in Large Language Models
evidence.summary: Benchmarks CoT monitorability across multiple model families (DeepSeek-R1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Kimi K2 Thinking, GPT-OSS-120B, Llama 3.3 70B, DeepSeek Chat v3) with cross-architecture comparisons; reports DeepSeek-R1 most monitorable on BBH/MMLU and that more capable models tend to be less monitorable, directly addressing whether monitorability is architecture/training-recipe specific.

evidence.title: Can Reasoning Models Obfuscate Reasoning? Stress-Testing Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
evidence.summary: Measures CoT obfuscation/monitorability across model families under pressure, finding strong family-specific differences (Claude models high external-CoT obfuscation, non-Claude families near zero), establishing that the CoT monitoring advantage is family/training-recipe specific.

evidence.title: OpenAI GPT-5 System Card (CoT-only vs CoT+Response monitor variants)
evidence.summary: The original source of the CoT-vs-output deception-detection result the proposal seeks to replicate; tests CoT-only and CoT+Response monitor variants on gpt-5-thinking with precision/recall, which the proposal aims to extend to open-weight families.

evidence.title: Monitoring Reasoning Models for Misbehavior and the Risks of Promoting Obfuscation
evidence.summary: Establishes that CoT monitors substantially outperform output/action-only monitors for detecting deception and reward hacking, the baseline claim the proposal builds on; shows the advantage and its fragility are already documented.
